There is a threat to exports of goods to the EU, which would harm exporters, and at the same time, imports may get more expensive from the EU if there are tariffs. On the other hand, it's in neither the EU's nor the UK's interest to have tariffs on trade, and being out of the EU, the UK can trade more freely with the rest of the world, which has benefits. There'll be uncertainty in the short term, but there is potential for long-term economic benefits. Another issue is movement of labour: if there are restrictions on EU immigration, businesses may find it harder to get the employees they need. On the other hand, fewer EU immigrants means more scope for immigrants from other parts of the world (I hope white countries, like Australia) who could fill jobs. Also lower-skilled British workers will benefit because they will not be competing as much for jobs, and they may get more pay. The UK can also benefit from being free of EU regulations: they'll still apply when exporting to the EU, but not for trade internal to the UK or exporting to outside the EU. These EU regulations may stifle business, although some of them are desirable regulations to protect things like the environment, workers' rights, or consumer safety.
